transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Dr. Eliza Moreno (Genehaven Head of Infra), Carlos J. (Lead DevOps), Ava R. (InfoSec), Tomoko S. (MLOps)

Summary: Quick intake around doing a fully air-gapped/private deployment inside Genehaven's controlled datacenter. Main concerns: how do we push updates without internet, how do we rollback model releases safely, hardware constraints (older PCIe lanes, mix of A100/H100 farm), KMS/HSM integration, attestation of images, and maintenance windows.

Topics: offline-update, image-signing, rollback-playbook, firmware constraints, model quantization for smaller GPUs, RBAC + audit logs

==== Transcript ====:
[00:00] Jordan: All right, hey team, thanks for taking time today. I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood. I think we have Priya on the SE side who will walk through the technical flow. Could folks on your side just intro quickly?
[00:08] Eliza: Sure, Eliza here. I'm head of infra at Genehaven, we run a datacenter pod in our facility in New Jersey. We have strict air gap — no outbound egress from the inference racks.
[00:14] Carlos: Carlos, lead DevOps. We manage the CI/CD for models and the image build pipelines, and we do manual USB-mediated pushes today for some internal tools.
[00:20] Ava: Ava, InfoSec. I'm going to be looking at KMS, signing, attestation, and audit retention.
[00:24] Tomoko: Hi, Tomoko from MLOps, focused on perf and canary criteria.
[00:27] Priya: Great, thanks. I'll try to surface how Redwood's private package maps to an air-gapped rollout and some of the constraints we usually see.

[02:05] Jordan: High level question — what's driving the move off hosted or dedicated? Is this regulatory or IP concerns?
[02:12] Eliza: Bit of both. We process genome sequencing outputs and derivations that are PII-adjacent. Our legal team is pushing for no external model hosting for production workloads. Also some stakeholders don't want dev/test bits touching the same network.

[04:10] Jordan: Makes sense. Timeline?
[04:14] Eliza: We have a compliance milestone end of Q3. Ideally we want a safe pilot in July, a constrained rollout by September. Budgets are... flexible up to an RFP threshold — we'd probably need dedicated/reserved pricing for GPU capacity.

[06:02] Priya: Quick note on model sizes and hardware — do you have H100s or older cards? That affects quantization and perf tuning.
[06:10] Carlos: Mixed fleet. 8x H100s per rack, but a handful of A100 40GB and some 80GB A40s; plus older 32GB Ampere boxes. We can't replace everything before pilot.

[07:30] Priya: Ok so we need to plan for heterogenous kernel selection and potentially per-node quantization. We can provide quantization profiles but in air-gapped mode we ship quantized artifacts as part of the package.

[08:12] Tomoko: How would updates work? Right now we have a strict patch window and everything is manually signed before we push.
[08:20] Priya: Two common patterns we've seen: 1) signed delta packages — you sign artifacts in your air-gapped signing appliance, generate a manifest, and import via removable media. 2) A sealed repository mirror where you physically transfer tarballs to a staging node that acts as a local registry. Both require image signing and verification on the host.

[09:03] Ava: Can Redwood integrate with our HSM (Thales) for signing or do we need a separate signing appliance?
[09:12] Priya: We don't directly touch your HSM. Typical flow: you use your HSM to sign the release artifacts; Redwood's package verifier checks signatures before accepting and flashing images. For attestation we support verifying signatures against your public keys.

[10:30] Carlos: We also have a strict requirement for immutable audit trails. We can't have opaque logs.
[10:36] Jordan: Redwood Console has per-route audit logs and token-level traces. In Private deployments we can push logs to your SIEM or write to a local write-once store.
[10:48] Ava: Write-once is important. Retention period is 7 years for a subset of events; we'll need to know formats and exportability.

[12:15] Priya: We'll provide a spec for the event types. For air-gapped deployments we can write logs locally and provide a signed compressed export that you can import to your long-term storage.

[13:40] Tomoko: On rollback: if we push a model that regresses, how quickly can we roll back given we can't pull from the internet?
[13:48] Priya: Rollback design is twofold: 1) Keep a ring of previously approved model artifacts on the node, signed and verified. 2) Use a promotion manifest that marks which model should be active. Rollback is simply flipping the activation manifest and reloading the KV cache.
[14:10] Eliza: But that assumes we pre-provision older artifacts. What's the storage footprint for keeping N previous models?
[14:18] Priya: It depends on model sizes. For example a 30B fp16 model compressed with our format might be ~60GB. We recommend keeping 2-3 previous versions on nodes with SSDs sized accordingly, or use a local model registry that nodes can pull from during maintenance windows.

[15:50] Carlos: Our racks have limited NVMe per node — around 2x1TB each. We won't be able to store many big models. Any options?
[15:58] Priya: You have a couple options: 1) Use sharded/quantized variants for older versions to reduce size, 2) Keep only lightweight rollback checkpoints (delta weights) that apply patches to a base image, or 3) provision a shared NFS/ON-prem object store accessible during maintenance windows. For strictly air-gapped constraints, delta patches and quantization are typical.

[17:25] Ava: We need cryptographic verification of patches — can Redwood support incremental patch manifests that are signed and include checksums?
[17:33] Priya: Yes, the update manifest includes per-file checksums and signature verification. In Private we run a local verifier that refuses unsigned or altered packages.

[18:45] Jordan: On the business side, how are you thinking about capacity? Is this per-request bursty or steady? That will influence Dedicated vs Private commit size.
[18:54] Eliza: Mostly bursty. We run batch jobs overnight, but interactive clinical review is daytime with tight p99 latency (under 300ms) for small seq queries. We also have unpredictable spikes during triage.

[20:10] Priya: Ok p99 under 300ms on mixed H100/A100 fleet is feasible if we tune batching and KV cache. For the offline batch jobs you can schedule scaled replicas during window.

[21:37] Tomoko: If we do Private, do we still get Redwood's rollout tooling like canaries and A/B?
[21:43] Priya: Yes. The control plane can be deployed in an offline mode where the controller runs locally. You get canary manifests, A/B splits, and automatic fallback policies — but in air-gapped mode all policies are evaluated locally against your manifests.

[23:05] Carlos: What about emergency fallback to hosted Redwood if our cluster goes down? We can’t allow data to leave network, so that might be a no-go.
[23:13] Jordan: Understood. A common pattern is to keep a sanitized model hosted as a last-resort read-only fallback with redactions, but for you that may violate policy. Another pattern is multi-region private replicas.
[23:35] Ava: We won't permit egress to hosted environments. We need fully on-prem fallback strategies.

[25:50] Priya: Operationally, we'll also want to discuss firmware level constraints — some older boxes have CPU microcode/BIOS limitations that break newer CUDA kernels. Did you have specific failures?
[25:59] Carlos: We observed a H100 driver crash on one of the older motherboards during a kernel update. We want a validated hardware matrix so we don't push images that brick nodes.

[27:10] Priya: Redwood maintains a kernel/kernel-config compatibility matrix and we can produce a validation checklist. For air-gapped installs we recommend pre-validating a golden node image that you can replicate.

[28:40] Eliza: How long is the image validation process? We have a short pilot window.
[28:46] Priya: Usually 2-4 weeks to validate across representative hardware if we need to generate optimized kernels. If you accept baseline kernels we can shorten that, but perf might suffer.

[30:20] Tomoko: On quantization — can Redwood produce INT8 variants we can ship, and will the inference fidelity degrade?
[30:28] Priya: Yes, we provide quantization profiles. Fidelity depends on model and task; we'll run evaluation sets as part of the PoC and provide regression metrics. For clinical tasks we've seen acceptable quality with certain 8-bit configs but we'll validate.

[32:00] Ava: Audit + compliance: we need role-based access control mapped to our SSO, and SAML is mandatory.
[32:07] Jordan: We support SAML/SSO and can integrate with your IdP. RBAC can be mapped to your groups. In Private we support local identity proxy if your IdP isn't reachable from the cluster.

[33:50] Carlos: How are secrets handled? We have a KMS/HSM. Will Redwood require secrets in the clear?
[33:57] Priya: No — Private supports integrating with your KMS. The agent running on nodes fetches ephemeral keys via an attested channel and never stores plaintext. For air-gapped setups we do a manual key provisioning step using your HSM public keys and a signed bootstrap token.

[35:40] Eliza: We need to know what audit fields are captured on inference requests — per-token logging is overkill for us, but we need per-request hash, model version, user token id, and decision flag.
[35:48] Priya: We'll supply a schema for required fields. You can pick retention and hashing strategies; we can redact sensitive fields at ingestion.

[38:10] Tomoko: On deployment frequency: we typically target fortnightly model updates. What's the recommended rollback shelf-life?
[38:20] Priya: Commonly 2-6 previous versions retained, but with delta patches you can keep smaller artifacts. If you only plan fortnightly updates, keeping 3 previous versions is a solid default.

[40:00] Carlos: Backup/restore: if a node fails mid-update, do you have atomic apply?
[40:06] Priya: The update is transactional: we write new artifacts to a staging area, verify signatures, switch the activation manifest, then warm the KV cache. If apply fails we revert to previous activation manifest automatically.

[41:55] Ava: Legal asked about evidence for signing and chain-of-custody for model artifacts. Can we get signed manifests with timestamps that we can store in our ledger?
[42:03] Jordan: Yes we can emit signed manifests with RFC3339 timestamps and signatures. We'll include that in the whitepaper.

[44:20] Eliza: What about resource controls — can we limit token cost per user or route-level quota enforcement?
[44:28] Jordan: Yes, quotas are configurable per-token/per-route and enforced locally in Private. We'll show examples in the console export.

[46:00] Tomoko: If we need a manual emergency rollback, what steps would our on-call need to perform?
[46:06] Priya: It should be a single signed manifest flip, then reload. We'll document the CLI incantation for your on-call and provide a playbook with exact commands for air-gapped ops.

[48:50] Carlos: Are there any pieces that require outbound connectivity at runtime — e.g., telemetry, license checks?
[48:55] Priya: No runtime outbound required. Telemetry can be buffered locally and exported during maintenance windows. License check is via signed tokens you provision; there's no live phone-home required.

[50:30] Ava: One more: we want to run internal benchmarks. Can Redwood provide a deterministic benchmark harness for locked-down environments?
[50:39] Priya: Yes, we can deliver a reproducible benchmark image and a small test suite you can run locally. We'll also provide perf expectation docs for each model variant.

[52:05] Jordan: To wrap, seems like key deliverables: whitepaper/SOC extract, offline update playbook, pricing ranges, and a plan for PoC validation across your mixed hardware. Anything else?
[52:15] Eliza: That covers it. We'll check budgets and send inventory.
[52:25] Ava: I'll follow up with a formal list of compliance controls.
[52:30] Tomoko: I'll share our evaluation prompts and target SLOs.
[52:36] Jordan: Great. We'll aim to send the docs by Friday, and set up a PoC planning call next week. Thanks everyone.

==== End ====
